paragraphs.source_en: By the time the escort bringing Toyotomi Hidetsugu and his party through Nara reached Seiganji Temple on Mount Koya, it was already evening on the tenth day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Bunroku. It was midsummer, and a smoky drizzle veiled the ridges and obscured the view.

paragraphs.source_en: When he had previously climbed the mountain beside the Taiko, Hidetsugu had still been the glorious regent. On that occasion, the monks who came to welcome him had filled the main hall of Seiganji. This time, however, even the holy man Mokujiki had excused himself from receiving him; in the monks' place stood countless soldiers surrounding the temple. Hidetsugu's mind was blank. He merely sat dazed in his palanquin, passing listlessly between the soldiers.
